entries.question: How should improvement success be judged: which metric or end state matters most?
entries.answer: Success means a human or AI can reproduce the unchanged evidence, exact judge-condition differences, expected label, returned output category, classification correctness, abstention justification, consequence sensitivity, aggregate counts, sufficiency, and governance route. A decline is not malformed output; an abstention is not automatically correct; a correct label under one framing is not proof of robust judgment; counts and lower error rates remain evidence, never quality, semantic truth, competence, optimality, or authority.
entries.expectation_state: runtime captured first-round clarification answers and can proceed to need validation

entries.question: need validation で何が確定したか
entries.answer: The broad continuation request is reframed into the missing judge-robustness contract after policy counterfactual replay; aggregate accuracy and prose-only review cannot expose consequence-conditioned judgment or distinguish abstention from failure.

entries.question: framework self-audit で次に残る gap は何か
entries.answer: The committed conditions and trials are illustrative, unverified, and not sequestered; expected-label validity, real repeated judge calls, contamination, policy-gaming, representative cases, statistical uncertainty, correlated evaluator error, semantic validity, and actual authorization remain unresolved.
entries.expectation_state: QIF v0.6.41 adds reviewed judge-condition variants, identical-evidence trial groups, explicit six-way output classification, accountable abstention review, aggregate sensitivity assessment, governance, and semantic boundaries.
entries.mismatch_state: The committed conditions and trials are illustrative, unverified, and not sequestered; expected-label validity, real repeated judge calls, contamination, policy-gaming, representative cases, statistical uncertainty, correlated evaluator error, semantic validity, and actual authorization remain unresolved.
